findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a non-blocking mechanism that actually excludes scanner-integration from the WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION all-jobs snapshot (e.g. gate the scanner child job's exit so it always concludes success while surfacing findings as annotations, or normalize WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION to disregard the scanner job's conclusion), and prove it by a job-conclusion-level test rather than actionlint, since caller-level `continue-on-error` does not mask the reusable child job's conclusion in list-jobs aggregation.
evidence: gerrit-verify.yaml vote job comment (lines 438-441): the workflow-conclusion snapshot 'folds the reusable workflow's job conclusions into WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION, so a clean-wheel/packaging failure casts Verified-1' — i.e. it reads the reusable's CHILD jobs, which a caller-level continue-on-error does not mask

normalize step CONCLUSION expression (lines 477-504): on a full route CONCLUSION resolves to `env.WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION`; a scanner-driven `failure` there flows through normalize_ci_conclusion.py (line 25-26) straight to VOTE_TYPE=failure -> Verified -1

The FAILURE_OBSERVED channel is safe (scanner is not in vote.needs, so not in `needs.*.result`), leaving WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION as the sole unguarded path — which continue-on-error on the caller does not close
actionlint checks workflow YAML syntax, not runtime list-jobs conclusion masking, so it cannot 'prove' the job is non-blocking as the plan asserts
findings.finding: The proposed non-blocking mechanism (`continue-on-error: true` on the scanner-integration reusable-workflow caller job) likely does NOT prevent a scanner failure from casting Verified -1, because im-open/workflow-conclusion aggregates the reusable workflow's CHILD job conclusions (not the caller job's masked conclusion) into WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION.
findings.location: Scope, para 2 ('the Stage-A scanner job must be non-blocking (`continue-on-error: true` on the reusable job, or an equivalent explicit wrapper proven by actionlint)')
scenarios: A patchset whose scanner lane finds a Semgrep/Gitleaks issue (or the scanner install fails) on the full route: the reusable child job concludes 'failure', WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION becomes 'failure', and Verified -1 is cast even though the change's real gates passed — recreating the vacuous/mis-blocking class the plan set out to avoid in Stage A

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify (via actionlint + a real GHA run, or a documented GitHub Actions reference) that the chosen non-blocking mechanism actually keeps the reusable-workflow scanner job's conclusion out of `im-open/workflow-conclusion`'s all-jobs snapshot; if `continue-on-error` is not honored on a `uses:` job, specify the concrete wrapper-job design (a normal job with steps that invokes the scanner and swallows non-zero) in Scope rather than leaving it as an unproven alternative.
evidence: Plan: "the Stage-A scanner job must be non-blocking (`continue-on-error: true` on the reusable job, or an equivalent explicit wrapper proven by actionlint) so a scanner failure is visible but cannot cast Verified -1"
gerrit-verify.yaml lines 438-441: im-open/workflow-conclusion "observes" the run's jobs via a REST list-jobs read — the mechanism whose interaction with a job-level continue-on-error is unproven
gerrit-verify.yaml scanner-integration would use `uses:` like build-and-test (line 233), optionality (line 262), mutation (line 245) — all reusable-workflow calls with NO continue-on-error

search_files: every `continue-on-error` occurrence in .github/workflows is at STEP level (test.yml, reconcile-bridge.yml, dependency-advisory-canary.yml, prompt-eval.yml, gerrit-verify.yaml vote steps) — no job-level-on-reusable precedent
Classification: Partially-verified — the reusable integration exists and its inputs match, but the specific non-blocking surface the safety design depends on is unconfirmed
findings.finding: The anti-90c7 non-blocking mechanism relies on `continue-on-error: true` applied to a job that CALLS a reusable workflow (`uses: ./.github/workflows/_scanner-integration.yml`), but GitHub Actions treats `continue-on-error` as a step-level construct and the allowed keys for a reusable-workflow-calling job do not include it; whether the flag parses and — more importantly — whether it keeps the job's conclusion out of the `im-open/workflow-conclusion` all-jobs REST snapshot is unverified. Every existing `continue-on-error` in this repo is step-level, so there is no in-repo precedent for the proposed job-level-on-reusable form.
findings.location: Scope ¶2 ("non-blocking (`continue-on-error: true` on the reusable job, or an equivalent explicit wrapper proven by actionlint)"); Anti-90c7 safety design
scenarios: Stage A lands; a real patchset trips a scanner finding; if the job-level flag does not neutralize the conclusion, im-open/workflow-conclusion folds the scanner failure into WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION and casts Verified -1 — the exact vacuous-block class the plan says it prevents
actionlint rejects `continue-on-error` on the reusable-call job, and the author has no concretely-specified fallback wrapper
